retrieved.title: FTC: How To Spot, Avoid, and Report Tech Support Scams
retrieved.excerpt:
Report it at ReportFraud.ftc.gov

How a Tech Support Scam Works

Tech support scammers use different tactics to trick you into believing there’s a virus or other issue with your computer.

Tech support scams often start with a bogus warning about a problem with your computer. It could be a fake pop-up warning that looks like it’s from a well-known company and urges you to call a phone number to get help.

retrieved.title: Safari pop-up guidance for iPhone
retrieved.excerpt: Safari pop-ups on iPhone can be ordinary ads or deceptive warnings. A warning, prize, or technical-support phone number displayed by a webpage is not proof that the phone is infected. If a pop-up is unfamiliar, avoid its links and buttons; even a close button may be fake. Close the Safari tab or window instead. To review Safari protection settings, open Settings, Apps, Safari, then check Block Pop-ups and Fraudulent Website Warning.

reference.title: FTC: Are Public Wi-Fi Networks Safe? What You Need To Know
reference.excerpt:
In the past, if you used a public Wi-Fi network to get online, your information was at risk. That’s because most websites didn’t use encryption to scramble the data and protect it from hackers snooping on the network.

retrieved.title: FTC: How To Secure Your Home Wi-Fi Network
retrieved.excerpt:
Turn on your router firewall. A firewall is an additional layer of protection that can help keep out viruses, malware, and even hackers. Most routers come with built-in firewalls, so check your settings to make sure your router’s firewall is turned on.

Protect your devices. Just as hackers can get to your data through unsecured networks, they can also get to your network through unsecured devices.
